questions.context:
Proteins are the most abundant biomolecules of the living system. Proteins are the polymers of about twenty different \(\alpha\)-amino acids which are linked by peptide bonds. Ten amino acids are called essential amino acids. In zwitter ionic form, amino acids show amphoteric behaviour as they react both with acids and bases.
On the basis of their molecular shape, proteins are classified into two types : Fibrous and Globular proteins. Structure and shape of proteins can be studied at four different levels i.e., primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary, each level being more complex than the previous one. The secondary or tertiary structure of proteins get disturbed on change of pH or temperature and they are not able to perform their functions. This is called denaturation of proteins.

questions.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
questions.context:
The involvement of \((n-1)d\) electrons in the behaviour of transition elements impart certain distinct characteristics to these elements. Thus, in addition to variable oxidation states, they exhibit paramagnetic behaviour, catalytic properties and tendency for the formation of coloured ions. The transition metals react with a number of non-metals like oxygen, nitrogen and halogens. \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) and \(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\) are common examples.
The two series of inner transition elements, lanthanoids and actinoids, constitute the f-block of the periodic table. In the lanthanoids, there is regular decrease in atomic size with increase in atomic number due to the imperfect shielding effect of 4f-orbital electrons which causes contraction.

questions.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
questions.context:
The involvement of \((n-1)d\) electrons in the behaviour of transition elements impart certain distinct characteristics to these elements. Thus, in addition to variable oxidation states, they exhibit paramagnetic behaviour, catalytic properties and tendency for the formation of coloured ions. The transition metals react with a number of non-metals like oxygen, nitrogen and halogens. \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) and \(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\) are common examples.
The two series of inner transition elements, lanthanoids and actinoids, constitute the f-block of the periodic table. In the lanthanoids, there is regular decrease in atomic size with increase in atomic number due to the imperfect shielding effect of 4f-orbital electrons which causes contraction.
questions.stem: In aqueous media, which is a stronger reducing agent — \(\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}\) or \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) and why ?

Attempt any five of the following :
(a) Write the IUPAC name of the complex :
\([\mathrm{Co(H_2O)(CN)(en)_2}]^{2+}\)
(b) Why is geometrical isomerism not possible in tetrahedral complexes having two different types of unidentate ligands coordinated with the central metal ion ?
(c) Arrange the following complex ions in increasing order of their crystal field splitting energy \((\Delta_{\mathrm{o}})\) :
\([\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}]^{3+}\), \([\mathrm{CoF_6}]^{3-}\), \([\mathrm{Co(CN)_6}]^{3-}\)
(d) Write the hybridization and magnetic character of the complex \([\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}]\) on the basis of valence bond theory.
[Atomic No. : Ni = 28]
(e) Out of \([\mathrm{CoF_6}]^{3-}\) and \([\mathrm{Co(C_2O_4)_3}]^{3-}\), which one complex is :
(i) more stable ?
(ii) the high spin complex ?
(f) What is the difference between an ambidentate ligand and bidentate ligand ?
(g) Write the electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{d^5}\) in terms of \(\mathrm{t_{2g}}\) and \(\mathrm{e_g}\) in an octahedral field when :
(i) \(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} > \mathrm{P}\),   and   (ii) \(\Delta_{\mathrm{o}} < \mathrm{P}\)

questions.stem:
(i) Calculate the \(\Delta_{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{G^{o}}\) and \(\log \mathrm{K_c}\) for the following cell reaction :
\(\mathrm{Fe\,(s)} + \mathrm{Ag^{+}\,(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Fe^{2+}(aq)} + \mathrm{Ag\,(s)}\)
Given : \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{Fe^{2+}/Fe}} = -\,0{\cdot}44\) V, \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{Ag^{+}/Ag}} = +\,0{\cdot}80\) V,
1 F = 96500 C \(\mathrm{mol^{-1}}\)
(ii) Write any two advantages of the fuel cells over primary and secondary batteries ?
(iii) How many Faradays are required for the oxidation of 1 mole of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) to \(\mathrm{O_2}\) ?
questions._flag: DEFECTIVE AS PRINTED, transcribed faithfully: the cell reaction in (i) is NOT BALANCED - it prints one \(\mathrm{Ag^{+}}\) and one \(\mathrm{Ag}\) against \(\mathrm{Fe} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\), so charge and silver are unbalanced; it should carry \(2\mathrm{Ag^{+}}\) and \(2\mathrm{Ag}\). Confirmed at magnification - no coefficient is present on either silver species, and the opener 56/3/1 carries the identical defect in its own Q31(b). CBSE's own marking scheme then solves it with n = 2, i.e. the scheme uses the balanced equation the paper failed to print. Separately, the printed split is 3+1+1=5 and the three sub-parts span three subtopics: (i) 'Nernst Equation' (filed here, the largest at 3 marks), (ii) 'Fuel Cells', (iii) 'Electrolytic Cells and Electrolysis'.

questions.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.stem:
(i) Write the major product(s) in the following reactions :
(1) Ethylbenzene \(\xrightarrow[\mathrm{b)\ H^{+}}]{\mathrm{a)\ KMnO_4\,,\ KOH}}\) ?
(2) Benzaldehyde \(+\ \mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3} \xrightarrow{\text{dil NaOH}}\) ?
(3) Benzoic acid \(\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2/FeBr_3}}\) ?
(ii) Give simple chemical tests to distinguish between the following pairs of compounds :
(1) Acetophenone and Propiophenone
(2) Pentanal and Pentan-3-one
questions._flag: The printed split is 3+2=5 and the parts span two subtopics: (i)(1) and (i)(3) are reactions of/producing carboxylic acids and (i)(2) is an aldol condensation, while (ii) is distinguishing tests for aldehydes and ketones. Filed on 'Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones'.
questions._figure: REQUIRED — five of the compounds in this question are printed as DRAWN benzene-ring structures (hexagons with inner double bonds) and are NAMED above rather than approximated: in (i)(1) a ring bearing \(\mathrm{CH_2CH_3}\) (ethylbenzene); in (i)(2) a ring bearing CHO (benzaldehyde), with its partner acetone printed out in full as \(\mathrm{CH_3-C(=O)-CH_3}\); in (i)(3) a ring bearing COOH (benzoic acid); and in (ii)(1) a ring bearing \(\mathrm{COCH_3}\) and a ring bearing \(\mathrm{COCH_2CH_3}\) (acetophenone and propiophenone). The whole of (a), stem through (ii)(2), sits on one page. Page idx 24.
